summary: The study describes the deposition of MoSe2 using a novel cyclic silylselenide precursor, 2,2,4,4-tetraisopropyl-1,3,2,4-diselenadisiletane, through thermal ALD. The process involves the reaction of the selenide precursor with MoCl5 at 300 /C14 C, resulting in high-purity MoSe2 nanosheets with out-of-plane orientation. The precursor was synthesized via a solvent-free method using elemental selenium and chlorosilanes, offering improved stability and volatility compared to previous selenium precursors.
evidence: The deposition of MoSe2 has been carried out in a custom-made thermal ALD system applying a deposition temperature of 300 /C14 C. The Mo precursor, MoCl5 (Strem, anhydrous 99.6%), and synthesized 6 were heated up to get sufficiently high vapour pressure at 120 and 155 /C14 C, respectively. The as-deposited MoSe2 structure was further characterized by means of Raman spectroscopy, X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), and grazing incidence X-ray diffraction (GI-XRD), confirming the out-of-plane orientation and high purity of the deposited MoSe2.
